p_553bb5e75f.title: 1.1 What is Victory Visual
p_553bb5e75f.content:
=== 1.1 What is Victory Visual ===
Victory Visual is a graphical visualization tool developed for working in conjunction with Silvaco TCAD and Atomistic simulators. It enables users to effectively visualize and analyze simulation results in 1D, 2D and 3D formats. Victory Visual accommodates both independent usage as well as integration with other TCAD interactive tools such as Deck Build, Victory DoE.

p_29ea033934.title: 1.2 Examining Data
p_29ea033934.content:
=== 1.2 Examining Data ===
Victory Visual empowers users to simultaneously inspect multiple data files. It offers the flexibility to visualize various types of data files, including logs and structural files. Users can effortlessly superimpose plots from different data files or choose to display them individually. Moreover, it facilitates interactive operations such as adding, removing, duplicating, overlaying, and isolating plots with ease.

p_6b7c931bb1.title: 1.3 Online Help
p_6b7c931bb1.content:
=== 1.3 Online Help ===
If the manual does not answer a particular question or a problem, you may contact Silvaco (support@silvaco.com) or use the Help Menu (see Section 2.2.6)

The following terminology is used throughout Victory Visual.

p_9c1ea0c80e.title: Table 1.1: Terminology
p_9c1ea0c80e.content:
=== Table 1.1: Terminology === [Table Data]:
ViewA sub window to the main window, used to display information about a file. This is the area where plots are shown. You can modify the arrangement of sub windows within the window: Views can be tiled and tabbed. The appearance of data can be set independently for each view.
StructureThis term is associated with data containing 1D, 2D, and 3D information about a simulated device, e.g., doping, geometry, materials, electric field profile, potential profile, carrier concentrations, etc. A structure is typically loaded from an str file, but the term can apply to all types of data that isn’t a plot.
PlotThis is one drawing or a graph plotted on axes at right angles showing relation between two quantities.
RegionA part of a structure that usually corresponds to a given material. It can be selected individually.

The Edit Menu provides control over the current view using operations that affect groups of plots as described below. There will be times when certain parts of the menu are greyed out. This happens when a specific operation is not applicable to the current group of selected plots / plot.

p_b07789f041.title: 4.1 Renderer
p_b07789f041.content:
=== 4.1 Renderer ===
In case of a black screen after opening a file or a crash, the renderer can be in cause.
There are different types of renderers available for Victory Visual. The render information can be accessed in the Help -> System -> Opengl Info section.

[Image Description]:
Based on the provided technical image and its context from the Silvaco TCAD user manual, here is the detailed analysis:

### 1. Device Type & Structure
* **Identification**: This image does not represent a physical semiconductor device structure (e.g., a FinFET or Planar NMOS). Instead, it is a graphical user interface (GUI) diagnostic window titled **"OpenGL Info"** from Silvaco’s 3D visualization tool, **Victory Visual** (or TonyPlot 3D).
* **Purpose**: This window is used to diagnose and troubleshoot rendering issues, black screens, or software crashes that occur when displaying complex 3D TCAD simulation meshes and fields.

### 2. Key Physical Parameters (System & Graphics Specifications)
The dialog displays key graphics interface parameters of the host system running the TCAD visualization software:
* **GL Vendor**: `VMware, Inc.` — Indicates that the software is running in a virtualized environment or utilizing a VMware-based virtual graphics stack.
* **GL Renderer**: `llvmpipe (LLVM 7.0, 256 bits)` — Specifies that a CPU-based software rasterizer (`llvmpipe`) is being used instead of a dedicated hardware GPU (such as NVIDIA or AMD). This explains potential performance bottlenecks when rendering large 3D structures.
* **GL Version**: `2.1 Mesa 18.3.4` — The OpenGL version supported by this driver configuration.
* **GL Shading Language Version**: `1.20` — The version of GLSL supported, which dictates the complexity of shaders that can be executed.

### 3. Axis & Data Values
Since this is a diagnostic dialog box rather than a data plot, the standard axes are replaced by text fields and user-interactive elements:
* **Data Fields**:
  * `GL_VENDOR` : `VMware, Inc.`
  * `GL_RENDERER` : `llvmpipe (LLVM 7.0, 256 bits)`
  * `GL_VERSION` : `2.1 Mesa 18.3.4`
  * `GL_SHADING_LANGUAGE_VERSION` : `1.20`
* **Interactive Controls**:
  * **Show Details...** button: Expands the dialog to show extended OpenGL extensions and driver capability parameters.
  * **OK** button: Closes the diagnostic window.

### 4. TCAD Command Context
* **Access Path**: This diagnostic utility is accessed inside the Silvaco visualization environment via the GUI path: `Help -> System -> Opengl Info`.
* **TCAD Diagnostic Utility**: When visualizing large 3D meshes generated by solvers like **Victory Device** or **Victory Process**, hardware-accelerated OpenGL is critical. If Victory Visual crashes or displays a black screen when loading a structure file (`.str`), engineers use this diagnostic window to verify whether the system has correctly bound to the hardware GPU or fell back to software rendering (Mesa `llvmpipe`), which may lack the required OpenGL features for advanced 3D rendering.

Opengl info pop up
Here is a list of the most common renderers:
Llvmpipe
Softpipe
OpenSWR
Hardware
If software mode is running (likely in most cases), Llvmpipe is the default renderer. Softpipe is a slow renderer and shouldn’t be used in any case. Do not set the GALLIUM_DRIVER environment variable manually. Unset it if need be.
It is possible to check the renderer directly from the terminal: glxinfo | grep "renderer"
OpenGL renderer string: llvmpipe (LLVM 7.0, 256 bits)
Sometimes it can be necessary to check the libraries associated with the rendering: rpm -qa | grep llvm

p_7804a6718a.title: Rendering speed on large structures
p_7804a6718a.content:
=== Rendering speed on large structures ===
Running Victory Visual using the –swr argument will set the OpenSWR renderer. victoryvisual -swr
This renderer can drastically improve the rendering speed of large structures (x20).
Another way to improve the framerate is to use a virtual machine. Don’t forget to enable hardware acceleration in the settings.
Virtual Box display setting, with hardware acceleration on
Switching off certain options can improve performance, see below.

p_6551f7a53b.title: 4.5 Opening large files
p_6551f7a53b.content:
=== 4.5 Opening large files ===
When opening a large file, a prompt will ask to open the file in quick mode, which is a mode allowing for a much faster loading time.

[Image Description]:
Based on the provided image and surrounding technical context, here is the detailed expert analysis and description:

### 1. Device Type & Structure
* **Software/Tool**: Silvaco **Victory Visual** (`victoryvisual.exe`), the interactive 2D/3D visualization tool for TCAD simulation results.
* **Structure Context**: Although the specific device structure is obscured in the background, the enormous file size (**5.92333 GB**) strongly implies a complex, high-density **3D mesh structure** (such as a multi-gate FinFET, GAA Nanosheet, 3D NAND flash memory cell array, or a large-area power device simulation) generated by **Victory Process** or **Victory Device**. 

### 2. Key Physical Parameters & GUI Features
* **File Size Parameter**: $5.92333\text{ GB}$.
* **Feature Displayed**: **Simplified Loading Mode** (Quick Mode). This dialog prompt automatically triggers when a user attempts to load a massive dataset that exceeds typical memory optimization thresholds, allowing the software to load a decimated or simplified version of the mesh to ensure fluid visualization and prevent system memory exhaustion (OOM).

### 3. Axis & Data Values
* **Dialog Box Components**:
  * **Window Title**: `victoryvisual.exe`
  * **Message**: `"You are opening a large file (5.92333 GB), would you like to use a simplified loading mode instead?"`
  * **Options**: 
    * `No` (associated with a red dot icon, typically loads the full mesh with all data points).
    * `Yes` (associated with a green dot icon, enables the fast/simplified loading mode).
* **Background Visuals**:
  * **Color Contour Map**: A spatial visualization using a standard rainbow color map (ranging from blue representing minimum values to red representing maximum values) is partially visible, indicating a field distribution such as potential, doping concentration, or electric field.
  * **Axes**: Partially visible axes boundaries on the left and bottom, with a fractional coordinate label `559` partially visible in the bottom-left text input field.

### 4. TCAD Command Context
This dialog represents an interactive GUI event during the post-processing phase. In a Silvaco DeckBuild run-file, this tool is typically launched using the following command structure after a simulation finishes:

```deckbuild
tonyplot3d <large_structure_file>.str -set <visualization_profile>.set
# Or launching directly via Victory Visual:
victoryvisual <large_structure_file>.vdb
```

When files scale into gigabyte ranges, the user is prompted with this choice to bypass loading complete mesh connectivity, accelerating initial render times inside the GUI.

Large file prompt

p_9037d54a31.title: 4.6 Using filenames with the ‘+’ character in them
p_9037d54a31.content:
=== 4.6 Using filenames with the ‘+’ character in them ===
With the victoryvisual command line arguments, the plus (+) is interpreted by default as a symbol to indicate an overlay of plot.
File names with the plus ‘+’ symbol in them are not supported by default in Victory Visual.
If you regularly use file names that contain a plus ‘+’, specify the --noplus option in Preferences

4.6 Issues
If you have issues to start the software, and the main screen is black before even loading a file, you need to wipe your preference folder:
rm -rf /path_to_config/.config/Silvaco
You can figure out this path by running the software with a special argument:
victoryvisual –settings=clear
And you should get the following output:
Clearing Settings ...
If it doesn't work, please delete the Silvaco folder manually : "/path_to_config/.config/Silvaco/VictoryVisual.conf"
Delete the whole Silvaco folder.

### 1. Device Type & Structure
* **Identification**: This image does not represent a physical semiconductor device structure (e.g., a FinFET or Planar NMOS). Instead, it is a graphical user interface (GUI) diagnostic window titled **"OpenGL Info"** from Silvaco’s 3D visualization tool, **Victory Visual** (or TonyPlot 3D).
* **Purpose**: This window is used to diagnose and troubleshoot rendering issues, black screens, or software crashes that occur when displaying complex 3D TCAD simulation meshes and fields.

### 2. Key Physical Parameters (System & Graphics Specifications)
The dialog displays key graphics interface parameters of the host system running the TCAD visualization software:
* **GL Vendor**: `VMware, Inc.` — Indicates that the software is running in a virtualized environment or utilizing a VMware-based virtual graphics stack.
* **GL Renderer**: `llvmpipe (LLVM 7.0, 256 bits)` — Specifies that a CPU-based software rasterizer (`llvmpipe`) is being used instead of a dedicated hardware GPU (such as NVIDIA or AMD). This explains potential performance bottlenecks when rendering large 3D structures.
* **GL Version**: `2.1 Mesa 18.3.4` — The OpenGL version supported by this driver configuration.
* **GL Shading Language Version**: `1.20` — The version of GLSL supported, which dictates the complexity of shaders that can be executed.

### 3. Axis & Data Values
Since this is a diagnostic dialog box rather than a data plot, the standard axes are replaced by text fields and user-interactive elements:
* **Data Fields**:
  * `GL_VENDOR` : `VMware, Inc.`
  * `GL_RENDERER` : `llvmpipe (LLVM 7.0, 256 bits)`
  * `GL_VERSION` : `2.1 Mesa 18.3.4`
  * `GL_SHADING_LANGUAGE_VERSION` : `1.20`
* **Interactive Controls**:
  * **Show Details...** button: Expands the dialog to show extended OpenGL extensions and driver capability parameters.
  * **OK** button: Closes the diagnostic window.

### 4. TCAD Command Context
* **Access Path**: This diagnostic utility is accessed inside the Silvaco visualization environment via the GUI path: `Help -> System -> Opengl Info`.
* **TCAD Diagnostic Utility**: When visualizing large 3D meshes generated by solvers like **Victory Device** or **Victory Process**, hardware-accelerated OpenGL is critical. If Victory Visual crashes or displays a black screen when loading a structure file (`.str`), engineers use this diagnostic window to verify whether the system has correctly bound to the hardware GPU or fell back to software rendering (Mesa `llvmpipe`), which may lack the required OpenGL features for advanced 3D rendering.

Based on the provided image and surrounding technical context, here is the detailed expert analysis and description:

### 1. Device Type & Structure
* **Software/Tool**: Silvaco **Victory Visual** (`victoryvisual.exe`), the interactive 2D/3D visualization tool for TCAD simulation results.
* **Structure Context**: Although the specific device structure is obscured in the background, the enormous file size (**5.92333 GB**) strongly implies a complex, high-density **3D mesh structure** (such as a multi-gate FinFET, GAA Nanosheet, 3D NAND flash memory cell array, or a large-area power device simulation) generated by **Victory Process** or **Victory Device**. 

### 2. Key Physical Parameters & GUI Features
* **File Size Parameter**: $5.92333\text{ GB}$.
* **Feature Displayed**: **Simplified Loading Mode** (Quick Mode). This dialog prompt automatically triggers when a user attempts to load a massive dataset that exceeds typical memory optimization thresholds, allowing the software to load a decimated or simplified version of the mesh to ensure fluid visualization and prevent system memory exhaustion (OOM).

### 3. Axis & Data Values
* **Dialog Box Components**:
  * **Window Title**: `victoryvisual.exe`
  * **Message**: `"You are opening a large file (5.92333 GB), would you like to use a simplified loading mode instead?"`
  * **Options**: 
    * `No` (associated with a red dot icon, typically loads the full mesh with all data points).
    * `Yes` (associated with a green dot icon, enables the fast/simplified loading mode).
* **Background Visuals**:
  * **Color Contour Map**: A spatial visualization using a standard rainbow color map (ranging from blue representing minimum values to red representing maximum values) is partially visible, indicating a field distribution such as potential, doping concentration, or electric field.
  * **Axes**: Partially visible axes boundaries on the left and bottom, with a fractional coordinate label `559` partially visible in the bottom-left text input field.

### 4. TCAD Command Context
This dialog represents an interactive GUI event during the post-processing phase. In a Silvaco DeckBuild run-file, this tool is typically launched using the following command structure after a simulation finishes:

```deckbuild
tonyplot3d <large_structure_file>.str -set <visualization_profile>.set
# Or launching directly via Victory Visual:
victoryvisual <large_structure_file>.vdb
```

When files scale into gigabyte ranges, the user is prompted with this choice to bypass loading complete mesh connectivity, accelerating initial render times inside the GUI.

Context Title: 1.1 What is Victory Visual
Content: === 1.1 What is Victory Visual ===
Victory Visual is a graphical visualization tool developed for working in conjunction with Silvaco TCAD and Atomistic simulators. It enables users to effectively visualize and analyze simulation results in 1D, 2D and 3D formats. Victory Visual accommodates both independent usage as well as integration with other TCAD interactive tools such as Deck Build, Victory DoE.

Context Title: 1.2 Examining Data
Content: === 1.2 Examining Data ===
Victory Visual empowers users to simultaneously inspect multiple data files. It offers the flexibility to visualize various types of data files, including logs and structural files. Users can effortlessly superimpose plots from different data files or choose to display them individually. Moreover, it facilitates interactive operations such as adding, removing, duplicating, overlaying, and isolating plots with ease.

The startup screen is shown bellow. On top of the Base Window, is the main menu bar that has the basic control menus for Victory Visual. The startup screen also consists of four options:
New File: creating a new file. Used in tandem with the slider panel or possibly the command panel.
Open: opening an already existing file. You can open multiple files using this. This can be done by selecting multiple files after clicking the “Open” option.
Open Overlaid: opening multiple files while overlaying them.
From Clipboard: saves the content of the clipboard (copied text) to a file and open it. The saved extension matters.

Context Title: 4.1 Renderer
Content: Opengl info pop up
Here is a list of the most common renderers:
Llvmpipe
Softpipe
OpenSWR
Hardware
If software mode is running (likely in most cases), Llvmpipe is the default renderer. Softpipe is a slow renderer and shouldn’t be used in any case. Do not set the GALLIUM_DRIVER environment variable manually. Unset it if need be.
It is possible to check the renderer directly from the terminal: glxinfo | grep "renderer"
OpenGL renderer string: llvmpipe (LLVM 7.0, 256 bits)
Sometimes it can be necessary to check the libraries associated with the rendering: rpm -qa | grep llvm

This logo represents the software suite environment used to simulate semiconductor fabrication processes and electrical device characteristics. In a Silvaco TCAD input deck (`.in` file run via **DeckBuild**), this branding is associated with tools such as:
* **ATHENA**: 2D process simulation (ion implantation, diffusion, etching, deposition, lithography).
* **ATLAS**: 2D/3D device simulation (solving Poisson's equation, continuity equations, and transport equations).
* **VICTORY Process / VICTORY Device**: Modern 3D process and device simulation engines.
* **TonyPlot**: The visualization tool where simulated device structures, meshes, and IV curves are plotted.

Context Title: Rendering speed on large structures
Content: === Rendering speed on large structures ===
Running Victory Visual using the –swr argument will set the OpenSWR renderer. victoryvisual -swr
This renderer can drastically improve the rendering speed of large structures (x20).
Another way to improve the framerate is to use a virtual machine. Don’t forget to enable hardware acceleration in the settings.
Virtual Box display setting, with hardware acceleration on
Switching off certain options can improve performance, see below.

Context Title: 4.4 File Auto Reload
Content: === 4.4 File Auto Reload ===
Sometimes a file modification will not be detected by Victory Visual.
In this case, it is necessary to enable the following setting:
Preferences -> Settings -> General -> Simple File Reload

Context Title: 4.5 Opening large files
Content: === 4.5 Opening large files ===
When opening a large file, a prompt will ask to open the file in quick mode, which is a mode allowing for a much faster loading time.

Context Title: 4.5 Opening large files
Content: ### 1. Device Type & Structure
* **Software/Tool**: Silvaco **Victory Visual** (`victoryvisual.exe`), the interactive 2D/3D visualization tool for TCAD simulation results.
* **Structure Context**: Although the specific device structure is obscured in the background, the enormous file size (**5.92333 GB**) strongly implies a complex, high-density **3D mesh structure** (such as a multi-gate FinFET, GAA Nanosheet, 3D NAND flash memory cell array, or a large-area power device simulation) generated by **Victory Process** or **Victory Device**.

Context Title: 4.5 Opening large files
Content: ### 2. Key Physical Parameters & GUI Features
* **File Size Parameter**: $5.92333\text{ GB}$.
* **Feature Displayed**: **Simplified Loading Mode** (Quick Mode). This dialog prompt automatically triggers when a user attempts to load a massive dataset that exceeds typical memory optimization thresholds, allowing the software to load a decimated or simplified version of the mesh to ensure fluid visualization and prevent system memory exhaustion (OOM).

Context Title: 4.5 Opening large files
Content: ### 3. Axis & Data Values
* **Dialog Box Components**:
  * **Window Title**: `victoryvisual.exe`
  * **Message**: `"You are opening a large file (5.92333 GB), would you like to use a simplified loading mode instead?"`
  * **Options**: 
    * `No` (associated with a red dot icon, typically loads the full mesh with all data points).
    * `Yes` (associated with a green dot icon, enables the fast/simplified loading mode).
* **Background Visuals**:
  * **Color Contour Map**: A spatial visualization using a standard rainbow color map (ranging from blue representing minimum values to red representing maximum values) is partially visible, indicating a field distribution such as potential, doping concentration, or electric field.
  * **Axes**: Partially visible axes boundaries on the left and bottom, with a fractional coordinate label `559` partially visible in the bottom-left text input field.

Context Title: 4.6 Using filenames with the ‘+’ character in them
Content: === 4.6 Using filenames with the ‘+’ character in them ===
With the victoryvisual command line arguments, the plus (+) is interpreted by default as a symbol to indicate an overlay of plot.
File names with the plus ‘+’ symbol in them are not supported by default in Victory Visual.
If you regularly use file names that contain a plus ‘+’, specify the --noplus option in Preferences

4.6 Issues
If you have issues to start the software, and the main screen is black before even loading a file, you need to wipe your preference folder:
rm -rf /path_to_config/.config/Silvaco
You can figure out this path by running the software with a special argument:
victoryvisual –settings=clear
And you should get the following output:
Clearing Settings ...
If it doesn't work, please delete the Silvaco folder manually : "/path_to_config/.config/Silvaco/VictoryVisual.conf"
Delete the whole Silvaco folder.
